### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**15** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **176** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c03a8a342805186e04e05d9903f7f1913b43dabe` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d061e50ab47e3ac98519c325a24f18885619ab18` — the merge of head `c5b827e5f3abfab7519e591419106419bbf19bf0` into base `c03a8a342805186e04e05d9903f7f1913b43dabe`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d061e50ab47e3ac98519c325a24f18885619ab18 && git checkout d061e50ab47e3ac98519c325a24f18885619ab18
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c03a8a342805186e04e05d9903f7f1913b43dabe c5b827e5f3abfab7519e591419106419bbf19bf0 && git checkout -B drift-repro c03a8a342805186e04e05d9903f7f1913b43dabe && git merge --no-ff c5b827e5f3abfab7519e591419106419bbf19bf0

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c03a8a342805186e04e05d9903f7f1913b43dabe
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `58464e71d4a2f09b814d24abadbfe2eaf4f1405a`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.stack-package-duplicate-entry-refused-at-every-door.ts + packages/objectql/src/engine-registration.ts
Security-touching: yes

Inputs read: card #35228 (body, 6 comments, ruling 7023505627, claim 7023784590, os-dev-report 7025836839), folded card #35608 (body, 2 comments), this PR's body, its 9-file list and the net diff against `main`, and the check-runs on the head as of 2026-11-20T00:14Z. The cited code was read in the tree at the head; nothing was built or run. The rest of the diff (five test files, the changeset) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

Verdict in one line: the three doors the ruling names are implemented with the #22934 wording and the A1 arm matches the ruling, so there is no must-fix. Three should-fix findings are open on this head (S1, S2, S3), all at the edges of the composition door, so a delta review is owed after their fix.

`Security-touching: yes` is meant, conservatively: the identity table this diff now reads at the composition and package-body doors includes `permissions`, `sharingRules`, `capabilities` and `positions`, so a same-package pair in those collections moves from last-wins to refused. No `hits` path is under `skills/**`, so the skills arm's label rule does not apply.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set changes the diff implies:

1. **Flat `composeStacks` (every manifest strategy but `'preserve'`), inputs' top-level entries judged together: 26 keys newly refused, `objects` skipped.** Right. This is the ruling's "on the output of `composeStacks`" and #35608's fold. `objects` stays with `objectConflict`, which is right: `mergeObjects` already refuses or folds a shared name.
2. **`defineStack({ packages })`: each `packages[i].manifest` body judged on its own, 29 keys including `objects`.** Right. The ruling names "every `packages[i]` body"; a body is registered by `registerApp` as a top level is.
3. **A composition's carried bodies, and under `'preserve'` the body each input with a manifest is assembled into.** Right. Reachable only through a `strict: false` input, and it keeps cross-package reuse apart (each body alone).
4. **A single stack: unchanged, byte for byte.** Right. Read in the diff: same key order, same `Array.isArray` skip, same origin spelling `stack.KEY[i]`, same sentence.
5. **The same entry object reached through two inputs counts once.** The accept set is unchanged from `main`, but the judgment is wrong against the registrar in this same diff: see S3.
6. **The flat door reads the top level of an input that itself carries `packages[]`.** Wrong: see S1.
7. **Under `'preserve'`, top-level entries that no body carries are judged by no door.** Accept set unchanged from `main`, but the claim "wherever the package is assembled" does not hold there: see S2.

Public-surface changes:

- No new export: every added function in `stack.zod.ts` is module-private.
- Error code for one shape changes: two inputs each declaring an app of one name were refused as `STACK_SINGLE_APP_VIOLATION` and are now refused first as `STACK_CROSS_REFERENCE_INVALID` (step 3b runs before 3c, the order `defineStack` uses). Right, and consistent; the changeset does not say it (nit N3).
- `@objectstack/objectql`: one new `error`-level log line per (package, target), with meta `{ package, target, entries }`. Nothing refused, nothing merged, `registry-object-registration.ts` untouched. Right against arm A1.
- Migration entry id `stack-package-duplicate-entry-refused-at-every-door` matches the changeset's `adr-0087: registered` line.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec` minor and `@objectstack/objectql` minor, with a BREAKING banner, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`. This matches what the diff publishes: it widens no accept set and adds no public export, and it narrows the accept set of `composeStacks` and of a `packages[i]` body. The gate's own rule (`scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`: `narrowed` beside a line without the `(narrowing)` arm is a contradiction; a narrowing ships `minor` in the launch window) agrees, and `Check Changeset` concluded success on this head. The `objectql` half is a log line only; `minor` is acceptable for it.

Clause-②: no (narrowing) — correct as written in the PR body and the changeset.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **open_questions 1 (which `Clause-②` spelling stands).** Option A stands: `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`. The gate refuses the other spelling mechanically and `Check Changeset` is green with A. The seat amends the `Clause-②: no` line of the claims on #35228 (7023784590) and #35608 (7023806340).
- **out_of_scope 1 (under `'preserve'` a manifest-less input contributes no body, so its entries are not judged).** Not accepted as "noted, not filed". It is #35608's own measure item 3 and it leaves the card's defect open at one door. Graded S2 below.
- **out_of_scope 2 (the A1 line is logged again on each registration of the same unfixed body).** Accepted, no carrier needed. The ruling asks for an error line while the body is unfixed, and a reload is a new registration.
- **out_of_scope 3 (the docblock still says 27 collections, the table holds 29).** Nit N1 below.
- **security_findings: none.** Agreed; nothing found in the scoped files.
- **Human Minimum item 3 unchecked (no local lint).** Answered by the head: `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · docs & code guards` and `Lint · repo & tooling gates` concluded success.
- **Two gate families the dev marked NOT MEASURED** (`check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`). Their CI lanes had no conclusion when this record was written: see the check-run note below.
- **#35608 "measure first" item 2 (boot census of the accepted keys) was not repeated.** Accepted: the composed top level reaches the same registrars #22934's census measured, and the pre-fix composition census (26 accepted with two entries) is on the PR.
- **SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5).** Not applicable: the diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join.
- **Check-runs on the head.** Concluded success: Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Spec property liveness, Dogfood Regression Gate, Lint · ESLint, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, the three scoped lint lanes, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Check PR Size. Still running, with no conclusion yet: Build Core, Test Core 1/10 to 10/10, Type Check · workspace, Type Check · consumer gates, Lint · CI, release & engine gates, and the UI lanes. This record does not vouch for those; the seat reads their conclusions before it acts. The PR is a draft.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts`** against ruling 7023505627, #35608, and its first consumers (the boot's package and residual registration).

What holds: one helper reads the table at every door, so the wording cannot drift; the sentence is the #22934 one; origins name the input or the body path as the claim's file surface asked; the refusals join step 3b, so they are `STACK_CROSS_REFERENCE_INVALID` and carry the inputs' conversion record through the existing `composeStacks` wrapper; two bodies are never compared with each other.

S1 (should-fix) — The flat composition door refuses legal cross-package reuse when an input carries `packages[]`. `collectComposedDuplicateEntryErrors` reads every input's top-level collections as "the ONE package a flat composition makes". That premise fails for an input that carries `packages[]` and a flattened top level, which `composeStacks` itself emits: a `'preserve'` artifact keeps the flattened copy whenever `packagesCarryEveryInputCollection` answers false (an input with no manifest, or an input carrying `packages[]` plus collections of its own). In that copy, two packages' entries under one identity sit side by side, for example two packages each extending `crm_line`, which is this PR's own accepted control. Nest that artifact in a flat composition and the door reports `stack #0 objectExtensions[0] and stack #0 objectExtensions[1]` with "only the last of these entries' fields register", which is false: the boot registers each body under its own id and does not register a top-level item a body declares (`unclaimedTopLevel`, mirrored in this file by `isResidualTopLevelItem`). The sibling check states the correct rule in its docblock: `collectComposedSingleAppErrors` says a nested artifact's flattened copies of its bodies' apps are not residual. The docblock of `duplicateEntryFindings` ("every door below hands it one package and nothing else, so cross-package reuse of a name is never read here") and the changeset's "Unchanged" bullet are therefore not true of this door. Read from code, not driven. Fix shape: for an input that carries `packages[]`, the flat door reads only the top-level entries no body of that input claims.

S2 (should-fix) — The residual package is judged by no door, so the card's defect survives under `manifest: 'preserve'`. Under `'preserve'` the flat door is skipped, and `collectComposedPackageBodyDuplicateEntryErrors` judges only carried bodies and inputs that have a manifest. Entries of a manifest-less input (and the own collections of an input that carries `packages[]`) reach only the composed top level. The boot registers those under the artifact's `manifest.id` as the residual, and its own docblock says two items of one name in one body register last-wins. So `composeStacks([defineStack({ manifest, objects }), defineStack({ pages: [home] }), defineStack({ pages: [home] })], { manifest: 'preserve' })` is still accepted with both entries in one package, and the same shape with two `objectExtensions` entries is the decision analysis's own example with one option added. #35608 asked for exactly this door to be checked (measure item 3), the ruling says "on the output of `composeStacks`", and the migration entry and changeset say "wherever the package is assembled". The dev disclosed it as an out-of-scope note with no carrier. Close it one of two ways: judge the residual (top-level entries no body claims) as one package under every strategy, which also gives S1 its fix; or file a card for the residual door before #35608 is closed and narrow the entry's and changeset's wording to the doors that are covered.

S3 (should-fix) — The spec door and the registrar disagree about one entry reached twice. `collectComposedDuplicateEntryErrors` counts one entry object reached through two inputs once and accepts the composition (pinned by "the same built sub-stack passed twice is one declaration"). The concat pass still emits that entry twice (`arrays.flat()`), so the composed stack, and any artifact built from it, carries two `objectExtensions` entries for one target. `logSameTargetObjectExtensions` counts by index, so every boot of that accepted composition logs at `error` that the fields of the other entry "are missing" and tells the author to "merge them and rebuild". Both statements are false there, a rebuild changes nothing, and the registrar's comment "authoring refuses that body now" is not true of it. The migration entry's acceptance criterion ("the boot log carries no error saying a package declares several `objectExtensions` entries for one object") fails for a composition this PR accepts, and the same output handed to `defineStack` as a `packages[i]` body after serialisation is refused. The docblock's "the boot loses nothing" is also not the whole account for `hooks`, where the table's own consequence line says every entry's handler is bound and runs. The three places must agree: the composition emits a twice-reached entry once, or the door refuses it, or the registrar's line does not fire on what authoring accepts.

N1 (nit) — The docblock above the table still says "the 27 collections" while the table holds 29 (`queues` and `assignmentRules` predate this PR). Fold it into the head that fixes S1 to S3, or leave it.

N2 (nit) — A flat composition of two inputs with two different manifests that reuse one name is now refused with "Rename one of them, or merge them". The refusal is right (one package results, and one entry was dropped at the boot), but the remedy does not mention `manifest: 'preserve'`, which keeps both, as the single-app finding does. Follow-up or accepted deviation.

**`packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.stack-package-duplicate-entry-refused-at-every-door.ts`** against its sibling `18.stack-collection-duplicate-entry-refused` and the ruling.

Shape, id and the no-conversion reasoning match the sibling, and the A1 arm is described as the registrar implements it. Its `replacement` ("wherever the package is assembled") and its `acceptanceCriteria` inherit S2 and S3 and are corrected with them.

N3 (nit) — The entry's `surface` lists `objects` among the composition's collections without saying that two inputs sharing an object name stay with `objectConflict` (the changeset says it), and neither text mentions that a same-name app pair now answers `STACK_CROSS_REFERENCE_INVALID` where it answered `STACK_SINGLE_APP_VIOLATION`. Prose only.

**`packages/objectql/src/engine-registration.ts`** (implementing file, arm A1), sentence by sentence against the ruling.

- "Logs an error naming both entries": yes. One `error` line per (package, target), naming the package, the target and every index, with the fix.
- "Keeps today's outcome, does not refuse the body": yes. The call sits before the unchanged loop and only reads.
- "Replace-on-reload is unchanged": yes. The extend splice is not in the diff, and the log is computed per registration, so a re-registration with one entry per target logs nothing.
- The logger call matches the contract's `error(message, error, meta)` signature, and the target it groups by is the same raw `extend` string the loop registers under.
- Its one disagreement with the contract is S3.

No must-fix. Open on this head: S1 (should-fix), S2 (should-fix), S3 (should-fix); nits N1, N2, N3.
